content.text: I want the git committer and author for any repos under src

I want the git committer and author for any repos under src/github.com/bookcreator to be thom@bookcreator.com and keep thom@tteggel.org for any other commits - what's the best way to achieve this without having to remember to update the local committer and author each time I check out a bookcreator repo?
I’ll check your Git configuration and add a directory-based identity rule for the Book Creator repos.

content.text: Git’s conditional includes fit this: keep `thom@tteggel.org` as the default, then override `user.email` for repos beneath `~/src/github.com/bookcreator/`. That sets both author and committer email for new commits, unless a repo or environment variable explicitly overrides them. I’m adding it to Home Manager so it persists across rebuilds.

text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"git diff --check; git diff -- home/home.nix; python3 - <<'PY'
import os, pathlib, subprocess, tempfile
source = pathlib.Path('home/home.nix').read_text()
assert 'condition = "gitdir:~/src/github.com/bookcreator/";' in source
assert 'contents.user.email = "thom@bookcreator.com";' in source
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='git-identity-', dir='/tmp') as directory:
    root = pathlib.Path(directory)
    include = root / 'bookcreator.gitconfig'
    include.write_text('[user]\n email = thom@bookcreator.com\n')
    config = root / 'gitconfig'
    config.write_text('[user]\n name = Thom Leggett\n email = thom@tteggel.org\n[includeIf "gitdir:~/src/github.com/bookcreator/"]\n path = ' + str(include) + '\n')
    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if not k.startswith(('GIT_', 'EMAIL'))}
    env.update(HOME=directory, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=str(config), GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM='1')
    for relative, expected in [('bookcreator/example', 'thom@bookcreator.com'), ('bookcreator/nested/example', 'thom@bookcreator.com'), ('tteggel/example', 'thom@tteggel.org'), ('bookcreator-other/example', 'thom@tteggel.org')]:
        repo = root / 'src/github.com' / relative
        repo.mkdir(parents=True)
        subprocess.run(['git', 'init', '-q', str(repo)], env=env, check=True)
        for role in ['AUTHOR', 'COMMITTER']:
            actual = subprocess.check_output(['git', '-C', str(repo), 'var', f'GIT_{role}_IDENT'], env=env, text=True)
            assert f'<{expected}>' in actual, actual
        print(f'{relative}: author and committer = {expected}')
PY","max_output_tokens":3000}));

text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"set -eu
identity_test_dir=$(mktemp -d /tmp/git-identity.XXXXXX)
trap 'rm -rf "$identity_test_dir"' EXIT
cat > "$identity_test_dir/bookcreator.gitconfig" <<'EOF'
[user]

EOF
cat > "$identity_test_dir/gitconfig" <<EOF
[user]
 name = Thom Leggett
 email = thom@tteggel.org
[includeIf "gitdir:~/src/github.com/bookcreator/"]
 path = $identity_test_dir/bookcreator.gitconfig
EOF
for relative in bookcreator/example bookcreator/nested/example tteggel/example bookcreator-other/example; do
  repo="$identity_test_dir/src/github.com/$relative"
  git init -q "$repo"
  case "$relative" in
    bookcreator/*) expected=thom@bookcreator.com ;;
    *) expected=thom@tteggel.org ;;
  esac
  for role in AUTHOR COMMITTER; do
    actual=$(env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME="$identity_test_dir" GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL="$identity_test_dir/gitconfig" GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 git -C "$repo" var "GIT_${role}_IDENT")
    case "$actual" in
      *"<$expected>"*) ;;
      *) printf 'FAIL: %s\n' "$actual"; exit 1 ;;
    esac
  done
  printf '%s: author and committer = %s\n' "$relative" "$expected"
done
git diff --check","max_output_tokens":1500}));
